basics.name: Jakub Tkaczuk
basics.label: Engineer & Researcher
basics.summary: Engineer and researcher with a PhD in cryogenics, alumnus of two EU H2020 programmes and the Marie Skłodowska-Curie network. Several years of R&D on scientific instruments and optimization techniques, applied to large-scale projects for the Future Circular Collider and the European Spallation Source in collaboration with NIST and Air Liquide. Now building low-cost instrumentation and appropriate technology for global health engineering at ETH Zürich.

work.name: Global Health Engineering, ETH Zürich
work.summary: Lead the biogas-sensing project and a team of research assistants developing low-cost biogas flow and composition sensors.
highlights: Lead the low-cost biogas flow & composition sensing project (patent pending)
Supervised around fifty BSc/MSc theses in mechanical engineering and thermodynamics
Introduced a group policy to publish hardware theses under a permissive CC-BY licence
Designed and equipped two mechanical workshops and a biological laboratory
Secured funding for biogas technology development in sub-Saharan Africa

work.name: Idiap Research Institute
work.summary: Worked with the speech-recognition team under the EU-funded ROXANNE programme, developing and integrating automatic speech-recognition models for a platform used by criminal investigators at Interpol.
highlights: Developed online speech-recognition engines and delivered solutions to commercial clients

work.name: CEA Grenoble
work.summary: Developed equations of state for mixtures of cryogenic fluids. Established accurate models for noble-gas mixtures through non-linear fitting followed by experimental confirmation, and extended the work to a helium–nitrogen equation of state for industry.
highlights: Reference equations of state for helium, neon and argon mixtures
Combined non-linear optimization with experimental validation

work.name: Air Liquide Advanced Technologies
work.summary: Developed the helium–nitrogen equation of state used for the process-cycle design of a Brayton-cycle refrigerator within the EASITrain H2020 programme.

work.name: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
work.summary: In the Thermophysical Properties of Fluids Group, collected and analysed data for equations of state of cryogenic helium, neon and argon mixtures, and assessed the feasibility of equations of state for quantum mixtures.

work.name: Technische Universität Dresden
work.summary: Worked on the Cryogenic Moderator System for the European Spallation Source (ESS): thermal calculations, equipment procurement, control-system design, and factory-acceptance-test planning for the complete cryostat and its liquid-hydrogen pumps, focusing on redundant pressure control under variable neutron load (APEX safety standards).

work.name: CEA Grenoble
work.summary: Studied magnetic refrigeration for the FCC-ee. Produced a feasibility study of kW-range superfluid-helium refrigeration down to 1.6 K for high-field superconducting RF cavities, and the conceptual design of a laboratory-scale prototype.

work.name: Copernicus Science Center
work.summary: Ran classes with students and teachers in crystallography, superconductivity, optics, magnetism, robotics and programming.

highlights: Dissertation: Equations of state for the thermodynamic properties of cryogenic mixtures
Thesis (with CEA and CERN): Preliminary conceptual design of a 1.6 K magnetic refrigerator for the CERN Future Circular Collider
Thesis (with GE Engineering Design Center): Analysis of the GE10-1 gas-turbine cooling system

awards.title: Patent pending — fluid composition and flow-rate sensor (EP25224614)
awards.summary: Low-cost remote-monitoring device based on thermal anemometry for measuring biogas flow, composition and overpressure in digesters, for carbon offsetting in low- and middle-income countries.

certificates.name: Learning Python for Data Analysis and Visualization
